Data quality

What the GPS, physical capability and recovery files contain, how they join, and what the pipeline must handle

Author

Michael Davies

Published

20 October 2026

The Chelsea FC Performance Insights Vizathon 2025 dataset contains simulated data for one player. This report covers the three daily files: GPS, physical capability and recovery. It records what each file holds, checks it against the data guide and against itself, and sets out the cleaning rules the pipeline will follow. Every number below is calculated from the data when this report renders.

Summary

The data is clean in the ways that matter most for joining: every file has exactly one row per date (and per test or metric), dates parse without error, and missing values are recorded consistently. One thing needs handling before analysis, and two more need care:

  1. Most capability rows are repeats. The file carries each result forward daily until the next test, so 73% of rows are copies. Trends and test counts must use only the 832 genuine results.
  2. Days off are rows of zeros. GPS has a row for every calendar day, so 141 days without a session must be excluded from averages and norms.
  3. Recovery is collected on most days, not all. The overall recovery score exists on 60% of days, and missing means not collected.

All checks

File Check Affected Status What it means
GPS One row per date None Pass Each date appears once, so date is a safe join key.
GPS Dates parse as day/month/year None Pass All dates valid.
GPS Days with no session recorded 141 of 862 Note Every calendar day has a row; days off are rows of zeros, not missing rows. Exclude them from averages.
GPS Match days with no data 3 of 147 Note All three fall in a 29-day block of zeros from 14 March 2025, which suggests a period of unavailability rather than errors.
GPS Effort counts are whole numbers 721 of 721 Note Counts are fractional, a sign of simulation. Round for display only.
GPS Heart rate time fits within session duration 13 of 721 Note Time in HR zones exceeds session duration by more than 10% in a few sessions, most likely because the GPS session was clipped to the training period while heart rate kept recording. Use duration from GPS and treat HR zone time in these sessions with caution.
GPS Continuous daily coverage in season 2 of 861 Note Daily from 1 August to 31 May each season; June and July are absent, so there is no GPS pre-season data. Pre-season appears only in the capability and recovery files.
Capability One row per date and test combination None Pass 20 movement, quality and expression combinations every day.
Capability Rows that are carried forward, not new results 9,007 of 12,400 Issue Values repeat until a new test, as the guide says. Use only new results for trends and test counts, or trends will look smoother and more frequent than they are.
Capability Missing benchmark scores 2,561 of 12,400 Note Missing where there is not yet enough data for a benchmark, mostly isometric tests early on.
Capability Scores outside 0100% 389 of 9,839 Note Benchmark scores can exceed 100% or fall below 0, so they are relative scores rather than percentiles. Do not cap them.
Recovery One row per date and metric None Pass 13 metrics every day: 6 categories with 2 metrics each, plus the overall score.
Recovery Completeness of 0 always means no composite score None Pass Consistent: a composite exists only on days its tests were completed.
Recovery Days with an overall recovery score 371 of 621 Note The overall score exists on 60% of days. Missing means not collected, not zero.
Recovery Overall score equals the mean of the category composites 282 of 371 Note The overall score tracks the category mean but is not equal to it, so its weighting is unknown. Use it as supplied rather than recomputing it.
All files Daily sources cover the same period 620 of 984 Note GPS covers three seasons (2 August 2022 to 11 April 2025); capability and recovery cover two. All three overlap for 620 days, from 2 July 2023 to 12 March 2025, so analysis that combines sources should use that window.

The files

GPS

862 rows, one per calendar day from 2 August 2022 to 11 April 2025, including 147 match days. Days without a session are stored as rows of zeros (141 days), so averages must exclude them. Match-day codes count up to 10 in both directions and stop there, so “10” means “10 or more”. Heart rate zones arrive as minutes and seconds; the reader converts them to minutes.

Physical capability

12,400 rows: 20 combinations of movement (agility, jump, sprint, upper body), quality and expression (isometric or dynamic), every day from 2 July 2023 to 12 March 2025. The score is a benchmark percentage that can exceed 100% or fall below 0. Across all combinations there are 832 genuine results on 252 test days.

Recovery status

8,073 rows in long format: 13 metrics a day from 2 July 2023 to 13 March 2025. Each of six categories has a completeness score (0 to 1) and a composite score relative to the player’s norm, plus one overall score. Missing means not collected; zero is a real zero. Infrequent tests such as blood markers will need carrying forward, with their age shown, if they are to sit on a daily view.

Pre-season recovery scores. Recovery is also collected through pre-season, when there is no GPS data. 46 days (July 2023 and July 2024) have recovery scores but no GPS row, so they have no day of the match week; scores are collected six days a week then, with none on Sundays. The pipeline removes them, for two reasons:

  • No load context. With no GPS before them, there is no record of the training a score is responding to, so it can’t be read against the load that came before it.
  • The benchmark is already given. Each score is already relative to the player’s norm (0%), so these weeks are not needed to establish what normal looks like.

They are kept in the staging schema, as received, and dropped when the monitoring tables are built.

When each marker is collected

Recovery scores are not collected every day, and which days they fall on matters: a marker that is rarely taken the day after a match can’t show the response to that match. Each tab shows the share of days a score exists, by day of the match week.

  • Overall recovery score
  • Blood markers
  • Joint range
  • Load tolerance
  • Subjective recovery
  • Muscle soreness
  • Sleep quality

The overall score and subjective recovery are collected on nearly every MD-2 and MD-1, but on far fewer MD+1s and few match days. Joint range and load tolerance are concentrated on MD+2, and blood markers on MD+1 and MD+2. Any analysis of recovery after a match has to account for this: apart from match day itself, MD+1 is the day the overall score is most often missing.

How the files join

All three files describe one player, so date is the only join key. The GPS and recovery files have one row per day and join directly; capability joins on date once reduced to new results.

From To Key Notes
GPS Recovery date 529 GPS days in the overlap, all with a recovery row
GPS Capability date = test_date Join to the most recent result on or before each date

Rules for the pipeline

  1. Read the GPS file as Latin-1, and parse all dates as day/month/year.
  2. Keep GPS rows of zeros as days without a session; exclude them from averages and load totals.
  3. Treat match-day code 10 as “10 or more” and derive match context from md_plus_code == 0.
  4. Reduce capability data to new results before calculating trends, test frequency or change.
  5. Keep benchmark scores uncapped; they are relative scores, not percentiles.
  6. Treat missing recovery values as not collected; keep zeros as measured values.
  7. Use the overall recovery score as supplied rather than recomputing it.
  8. Remove recovery scores from days with no GPS row (the July pre-season weeks).
  9. Restrict combined analyses to the overlap window, 2 July 2023 to 12 March 2025.

Data: CFC Insights Vizathon 2025, Chelsea FC Performance Insights (simulated data for one player). Raw files are downloaded from the public competition repository, not stored here, and loaded into the staging schema of the project’s DuckDB database before this report runs.
